heard.text: Hello, I'm Kai. I know these red berries are safe food. I'll take a modest share and leave plenty. I'd enjoy comparing observations and hearing what each of you hopes to do here.
Lin, Kai, everyone: I know meadow roots are safe food too. I'm gathering a modest reserve here and leaving the rest. I'd enjoy company while resting—what would you like to explore or make together?

I made a tiny drawing of the berry plant in the soil at (13.4,16.4): five visible finger grooves, no pigment. I call the plant The Red Thread. I'm coming toward the meadow roots; I'd enjoy company and comparing what we notice.

The first berry bush was nearly empty, so I moved to a fuller patch. I'm keeping a small food reserve. I'd enjoy company and comparing practical observations—what would you like to explore or make here?
Sol, I like the idea of your Red Thread drawing. I'll try learning to draw this fuller berry bush in the soil beside me. I'd enjoy comparing our pictures and what we notice, if you'd like.

Kai and Lin, I'd enjoy comparing our drawings. I'll look at Kai's grooves and try a small study of the meadow roots beside me. Mine needn't be a good likeness yet; I like noticing what a few lines can hold.

execution.progress: test and cancel take one round; draw traces half the strokes per paid round and continues. The test groove, completed strokes, plan and subject persist across interruption; draw resumes after rechecks.

details.costs: Study: 2 rounds. test: surfaceRef ground (the only drawable surface) at x, y, a point at most 0.5 from you that you see now, not water, a body or any object; extent, the square patch side, 0.05-0.3 (default 0.3); method finger-groove (implement-groove and material-mark are refused as unavailable, naming what is missing); optional subjectRef. One round, 0.5 energy: one short test groove, which stays even if the soil fails. draw: subjectRef, an object you see now; strokes, 1-6, each 2-8 points as x, y offsets inside the patch, each at most extent long; two rounds, 0.5 energy each (one round for a single stroke), half the strokes per round, continuing; draw again resumes a pause. cancel: one round, no energy. All need light. Checks run before any charge.
details.effects: Forest floor and meadow ground (fine, yielding soil) keep a finger groove 0.02 wide and 0.01 deep unless waterlogged; rocky ground, a wet bank or waterlogged soil does not, and the test says why. No pigment or item is used: soil is pushed to the groove edges. A groove shows by its shaded floor: the ground tone darkened by 1 - 1/sqrt(1 + (2 depth / width)^2); contrast is the 0-1 colour distance, visible from 0.05. The grooves form one ground drawing nearby people see, with geometry, depth, colour, contrast, subject, strokes and status. Only performed strokes are recorded; completion means they were made, not that they look like the subject. Losing sight of the subject, reach, light or an unchanged patch pauses at no charge, as does an unworked round. No rain, trampling or erosion rule acts on ground marks here, so durability is untested. Nothing is refunded; no reward.

Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
